stemMd: The primary purpose of the passage is to
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of the passage only.

options.label: A
options.textMd: recommend that cities abandon canopy targets in favour of other forms of cooling for dense streets

options.label: B
options.textMd: argue that the way a canopy target is defined and measured can decide whether it helps the residents most exposed to heat

options.label: C
options.textMd: show that satellite data has made street-by-street canopy targets cheaper to meet than city-wide ones

options.label: D
options.textMd: explain why street trees lower surface temperatures more cheaply than other forms of climate adaptation

options.label: E
options.textMd: compare the cost of planting in parks with the cost of planting in narrow streets

explanationMd:
Ask what every paragraph is working towards. The first paragraph sets up canopy targets as attractive. The second shows that a city-wide percentage can be met without helping the hottest districts. The third weighs street-level targets and the objections to them. The fourth argues that counting trees planted, rather than canopy that survives, rewards the wrong thing.

Each paragraph is about **how the target is defined or measured** — city-wide versus street by street, trees planted versus canopy that lasts — and about whether that definition reaches the people who need shade most. That is the choice describing the passage as an argument about how targets are defined and measured.

**How to check.** A primary-purpose answer must cover the whole passage and match its stance. The cooling-cost point appears only in the first paragraph, the cost comparison is one clause of the third, and the passage never tells cities to give targets up.

distractorRationale.d: The cheapness of canopy is mentioned in the opening paragraph as the reason targets are popular. It is background for the argument, not its purpose; three of the four paragraphs are about how targets are set and measured.
distractorRationale.a: The passage criticises how targets are framed but never proposes abandoning them. Its last paragraph proposes measuring canopy that survives, which is a better target, not no target.
distractorRationale.e: Planting costs appear only in passing: parks are cheapest, and narrow streets need soil cells. A cost comparison is a detail used in the argument, not the point of the passage.
distractorRationale.c: The passage says satellite data makes street-level targets cheaper to MONITOR, which weakens one objection. It says nothing about them being cheaper to MEET, and this is not the point of the whole passage in any case.

accessibilityText: A question about the passage on urban tree-canopy targets. It asks for the primary purpose of the passage. The five options complete the sentence: arguing that how a target is defined and measured decides whether it helps those most exposed to heat; explaining why trees cool cheaply; recommending abandoning canopy targets; comparing planting costs in parks and narrow streets; showing satellite data makes street-level targets cheaper to meet.

provenance.notes: Original item. Each distractor is a detail of one paragraph, an overstatement of the author's stance, or a distortion of what the satellite data changes.
